headline: India Revises Validity Periods For Pollution Under Control Certificates
seoTitle: India Revises PUC Certificate Validity Regulations
metaDescription: India has updated its regulations for vehicle emissions testing, introducing new validity periods for PUC certificates based on vehicle age and standards.
aiSummaryBullets: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways introduced updated regulations for Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate validity.
BS-VI vehicles receive extended renewal intervals based on their age, while older vehicle categories now have standardized testing timelines.
Vehicles meeting BS-VI standards that are over 10 years old are now required to undergo emission testing every six months.
aiContextParagraph: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in India has officially implemented new guidelines regarding the validity of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates for motor vehicles. These regulatory updates aim to standardize the emission testing process across the country for different vehicle emission norms, ranging from BS-I to the current BS-VI standards. According to the new mandate, newer BS-VI compliant vehicles will benefit from extended validity periods for their pollution certificates, allowing for less frequent checks in their early years of operation. Conversely, the government has imposed stricter mandates for older vehicles and established frequent testing requirements for BS-VI vehicles once they exceed a 10-year age threshold. These measures are designed to ensure consistent monitoring of vehicular emissions and enforce compliance with environmental standards, impacting a broad spectrum of vehicle owners across the nation by streamlining the renewal cycle.
